purpose: Canonical vocabulary for Swell pages, guides, schema, internal links, sales language, and answer-surface measurement.
usageRules: Use the preferred term as the page or section's primary label; introduce aliases as reader language, not separate invented categories.
Link a term to its canonical URL when the definition materially helps the reader.
Do not imply that a technical artifact, crawler permission, structured-data change, or content format guarantees inclusion, ranking, or citation.
Keep observed answers, supported claims, hypotheses, and causal conclusions distinct.

terms.definition: A digital agency whose research, production, orchestration, measurement, and knowledge systems are designed around governed AI workflows rather than added as isolated tools.

An operating model in which verified workflows can advance work across acquisition, onboarding, campaigns, reporting, and follow-up within explicit scope, consent, budget, quality, and approval boundaries.
A versioned marketing process in which an agent can interpret state, use approved tools, produce evidence, and select permitted next actions under defined policy.
The governed coordination of audience, assets, channels, approvals, tracking, budgets, stop conditions, measurement, and follow-up around one campaign objective.
A required, recorded decision by an authorized person before an agent can make a material commitment or execute an action outside autonomous policy.
The lifecycle, policy, event, approval, and action layer that coordinates multiple systems without treating any single AI product as the source of truth.

A disclosed conversational interface that can answer approved questions, capture buyer context, route requests, and recommend verified next steps without impersonating a human or inventing commitments.
A measurement practice that connects source, acquisition, sales, delivery, retention, and feedback events so later outcomes can improve future decisions.
The practice of improving the clarity, accessibility, evidence, and corroboration that generative answer systems can use when representing an entity or topic.
A broader practice of structuring information so search and answer products can resolve a question directly; it overlaps with GEO but is not an automatic synonym in every context.
The observed presence and treatment of an entity, claim, or source in defined AI-assisted search and answer experiences.
The ongoing discipline of aligning what an organization can prove with how answer systems describe, attribute, and cite it.
A material difference between an observed answer and the current representation an organization can support with evidence.
A versioned record of queries, conditions, answers, inclusion, accuracy, attribution, citations, and alternatives before or between interventions.
The earliest verified failure across entity definition, access, evidence, corroboration, or measurement that should be resolved before downstream work.
The work of making an organization, person, product, location, or concept unambiguous and consistently connected to supportable attributes and relationships.
The degree to which a reader or system can distinguish an entity from similarly named, previous, parent, sibling, or related entities.
The documented set of canonical entities, identifiers, attributes, and verified relationships used consistently across owned and relevant external sources.
The authoritative identity record selected for one real organization, person, product, place, or concept, with a stable identifier and source.
A structured network of entities and relationships. Public and private knowledge graphs vary, so schema markup should describe verified facts rather than presume adoption by a specific graph.
Machine-readable markup that expresses page entities and properties using a shared vocabulary such as Schema.org; JSON-LD is one common syntax.
A Schema.org property used to identify another URL that represents the same entity—not a parent, partner, sibling, author, or merely related organization.
The effective ability of a documented crawler or user-directed fetcher to retrieve a public resource under the publisher's directives and infrastructure controls.
The process by which a system locates and selects information relevant to a request; public optimization work can improve accessible evidence but cannot guarantee a system will retrieve it.
A proposed plain-text guide to important public site content. It can aid orientation but is not an access-control standard or a guaranteed ranking signal.
The degree to which a claim is explicit, attributable, accessible, current, scoped, and supported well enough to be inspected and potentially cited.
Content that makes useful, supportable claims clear and inspectable for readers and systems without manufacturing authority or guaranteeing citation.
Content structured so a bounded question can be answered clearly in context; answer readiness is a usability property, not proof of authority or future inclusion.
Content whose material claims are connected to appropriate sources, provenance, scope, ownership, and review dates.
A governed record connecting each material claim to source evidence, canonical publication, owner, status, and review date.
Relevant support from a source outside the entity making the claim, evaluated for independence, quality, scope, and recency.
A source reference presented by an AI-assisted answer product. Citation behavior differs by product, mode, query, date, and conditions.
The proportion of a versioned query portfolio for which a specified entity or source is cited under documented observation conditions.
The degree to which observed material claims match the current evidence available for the intended entity and scope.
Whether an observed answer assigns a claim, product, credential, or relationship to the correct entity.
A versioned set of commercially relevant category, problem, comparison, and verification questions used for repeatable observation.
A portfolio-level measure of how often an entity appears in defined answer observations. The denominator, products, prompts, dates, and counting rules must be disclosed.
A versioned record connecting interventions to later answer observations while separating observed change from unproven causality.
